about: The measurement corpus (docs/measurement.md). development: tuning and eyeballing allowed. holdout: never read while tuning; run it when a release note is about to claim the tool got more effective. well-kept: chosen before running anything, by an outside criterion. large: repositories too slow or too big for the development loop, run in release rounds only (`run --release`). awkward and gate: fixtures the harness builds.

series.note: the development set every release since 0.2.0 was measured on; the history's long graphs are drawn over these four, so a change to the development set does not read as a move. The dashboard and the per-release table use the whole set.

well_kept_criterion: CNCF graduated projects (cncf.io/projects, graduated maturity), four Go projects of moderate size; chosen on 18 September 2026 before any gitmole run on them
development_criterion: Chosen by the maintainer, 26 September 2026. Medium: on the pinned commit, the record's `seconds` at most 120 and `peak_mb` at most 1,500, each the median of three runs (a member: its last three release records; a newcomer: three scratch runs), with tracked text under the duplicates step's 80 MB budget. Sticky exit: a member is considered for leaving only after two consecutive release records exceed the bound, and the maintainer decides. Diverse: at least one medium repository each for C, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, Ruby and Rust where one passes; Go is covered by the well-kept set. Replacements were picked in the order of a saved GitHub search (>= 5,000 stars, created before 2022-09-26, pushed after 2026-06-01, 10-150 MB), skipping owner apache, reserve entries and corpus members, at most five clones per language, requiring >= 50% of scc code lines in the language and a clean ranking (six cut-offs, best 15 each), headroom unseen.

moves.note: the ApacheJIT repositories were read once, for the watch list's ranking decision (validation.md); nothing was tuned against them, so they stay the holdout

ghidra (the maintainer's review commit) and binutils-gdb join the development set: three repositories gave intervals too wide to show a move, and the Ghidra-derived rules needed a second repository. Records before 0.27.0 hold three development repositories plus gitmole, so their medians are not comparable with later ones without a rerun.

the development set becomes medium and diverse, by the maintainer's decision (development_criterion). django (165 s, the median of its last three release records), ghidra and binutils-gdb (376 s) move to the new large set, run in release rounds only; redis, tokio, jadx (Java), brew (Ruby) and yt-dlp (Python) join; curl, react and gitmole are grandfathered. The Ghidra-derived rules (imports, vendoring, notices, generated parsers) are now exercised in release rounds only. Measured on this corpus with 0.36.0 in a scratch release round (loads 3.8 to 10.7): the development cost ceilings re-base to a findings median of 19.5 and p90 of 25.8 (from 23.5 and 28.0: smaller repositories, not a better tool), report lines 216 (220.5), timed seconds 415 (766) and peak memory 1,251 MB (from 1,130: a raise, from redis, decided with the set); the large set's ceilings are 531 s and 1,121 MB. Effectiveness now spans development and large: headroom 0.657 [0.458, 0.831] on this corpus against 0.617 on the old set is a different population, not a move. A loop (development, awkward, gate) times 445 s; a release round is about 22 minutes. series is unchanged and keeps django. The loop's labelled share reads lower until the new repositories are labelled. django ran in 92 s in this round: it can rejoin if its release-record median falls under the bound.
